children: Canadian forestry products company Interfor warns that lumber market volatility is likely to persist into 2027. Shares are down 13% to C$12.85. Interfor says that seasonal pricing declines and mounting trade headwinds are also likely to be fixtures in the short-term, pointing to a 6% and 11% decline in prices for Western SPF and Southern Yellow Pine, respectively. Compounding the pressure, management cautions that near-term turbulence will be exacerbated by steep U.S. duties on Canadian lumber, oil prices, Section 232 tariffs and shifting monetary policy. On the brighter side, Interfor notes that roughly 65% of its output is produced and sold directly within the U.S., leaving only about 20% exposed to cross-border duties. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)
